claude-hackathon.title: Hacking Human Ability: Taking First Place at Superhuman Lab

photos.caption: Bagging first place trophy with the team at TinkerSpace Calicut
Hardware prototyping setup, wire harnesses and CAD testing

claude-hackathon.excerpt: Our team just bagged first place at the Superhuman Lab hackathon at TinkerSpace Calicut! We spent the first weekend of October completely immersed in this event, and it wasn't your usual demo-day...
paragraphs: Our team just bagged first place at the Superhuman Lab hackathon at TinkerSpace Calicut! We spent the first weekend of October completely immersed in this event, and it wasn't your usual demo-day theater. The whole goal was to hack human ability by using AI and hardware to turn assistive tech into actual upgrades instead of just basic medical devices. It was an amazing environment with engineers, designers, and people with lived experiences sitting down together to build prototypes that actually matter.

After 48 hours of heavy CAD modeling, wiring up microcontrollers, and surviving on basically zero sleep, seeing our project take the top spot felt incredible. It was the perfect chance to put my usual electronics and 3D printing tinkering into something with a real, tangible impact. Really proud of everyone on the team for pulling this build together over the weekend.

walking-ferns.excerpt: Spending the day volunteering with Walking Ferns was a great experience. The initiative focuses on experiential, outdoor learning, helping kids build curiosity by getting them out of formal class...
paragraphs: Spending the day volunteering with Walking Ferns was a great experience. The initiative focuses on experiential, outdoor learning, helping kids build curiosity by getting them out of formal classrooms and into nature. It was really interesting to step into a mentoring role in such an unstructured environment, where the focus is on letting children explore and figure things out hands-on rather than just feeding them information.

The day was a mix of quiet indoor moments and a lot of outdoor energy. We spent time sitting on the floor in group huddles for shared activities, but the highlight was definitely getting outside and climbing trees with the kids. It was a very grounded, community-driven space, and just hanging out in the branches and taking group selfies with the parents and children made the whole learning process feel completely natural and fun.

useless-project.title: Why I Built a Useless Cyber-Glove (And Won Second Place)

photos.caption: Wearing the chaotic latex cyber-glove wired with microcontrollers and jumpers
Debugging serial signals and firmware on the laptop workbench

useless-project.excerpt: I just grabbed second place this weekend at Useless Projects 3.0, which turned out to be exactly what a maker event at TinkerSpace Calicut should look like. Hosted by TinkerHub, the whole premise...
paragraphs: I just grabbed second place this weekend at Useless Projects 3.0, which turned out to be exactly what a maker event at TinkerSpace Calicut should look like. Hosted by TinkerHub, the whole premise of the hackathon was to celebrate the joy of building things purely for fun, without worrying about whether they actually solve a real-world problem. It was great to see such a solid group of creators show up, spending the weekend experimenting, breaking things, and showing off some genuinely quirky ideas in a totally pressure-free environment.

My entry for the weekend was a wonderfully impractical wearable hardware setup. I strapped a microcontroller to my wrist, ran a bunch of exposed jumper wires down a latex glove, and spent way too long actively debugging the whole thing on my laptop. It took some seriously chaotic hardware hacking to get it running, but the messy build process completely paid off in the end. Taking home a prize for something intentionally useless was a pretty amazing way to wrap up the weekend.

nit-physics-visit.title: A Day at NITC: Inside the Advanced Physics Labs

photos.caption: Inside the advanced physics lab with precision superconducting instrumentation
Inspecting specialized materials chemistry and applied polymer setups

nit-physics-visit.excerpt: Our recent industrial visit to the Department of Physics at NIT Calicut offered an excellent look into the practical side of advanced physical sciences. The department clearly prioritizes high-le...
paragraphs: Our recent industrial visit to the Department of Physics at NIT Calicut offered an excellent look into the practical side of advanced physical sciences. The department clearly prioritizes high-level research, which was evident from their strong focus on publishing in specialized fields like materials chemistry and applied polymers. It was inspiring to experience an academic environment so deeply committed to pushing the boundaries of fundamental and applied physics, while actively preparing students to step into innovation and leadership roles within the scientific community.

The absolute highlight of the tour was getting to see the department's high-end instrumentation firsthand. Walking into the lab and observing the JEOL 500 NMR spectrometer in person really put our theoretical studies into perspective. This sophisticated, superconducting equipment is crucial for complex molecular characterization and structural analysis. Having the chance to see the real-world infrastructure required to run such advanced spectroscopy experiments gave us a much better understanding of what it actually takes to conduct professional, cutting-edge research.

nss-state-camp.excerpt: The NSS State Level Leadership Camp wrapped up after a busy three days at CM College of Arts and Science. Held from October 17th to 19th, 2025, the event brought together student volunteers under...
paragraphs: The NSS State Level Leadership Camp wrapped up after a busy three days at CM College of Arts and Science. Held from October 17th to 19th, 2025, the event brought together student volunteers under the University of Calicut and the Kerala Higher Education Department. Things kicked off with an introductory session where local police officers spoke to the crowd about stepping up as youth leaders and taking responsibility in their communities. The main goal of the weekend was to take the NSS motto of "Not Me But You" and turn it into practical skills, giving volunteers a space to figure out how to manage projects and communicate better when they get back to their home units.

Over the three days, the schedule was packed with a mix of indoor discussions and outdoor team-building sessions. Instead of just sitting through lectures, volunteers spent time out in the field working on group tasks, which really helped break the ice and build connections among students from all over the state. Evenings usually shifted toward cultural programs and open panels where everyone could share what was actually working in their local community drives. By the time the closing session rolled around, the volunteers were heading home with a lot more confidence, a solid network of friends, and a clearer game plan for their upcoming campus initiatives.

nss-university-camp.excerpt: From March 22 to 24, 2025, the University of Calicut's NSS department hosted a three-day residential camp called "Calicut Swachhata". The event brought together 100 volunteers selected from 100 d...
paragraphs: From March 22 to 24, 2025, the University of Calicut's NSS department hosted a three-day residential camp called "Calicut Swachhata". The event brought together 100 volunteers selected from 100 different colleges across the region. The camp kicked off with an inauguration and featured several seminars focused on waste management and everyday cleanliness. Along with these sessions, a typical camp like this would also include morning warm-ups, ice-breaker games, and evening cultural programs where students get to showcase their talents and bond with volunteers from other colleges.

The main highlight of the three days was the "Destination Swachhata" campaign, where the students headed out for a major beach cleaning drive at Chaliyam Beach. Working under the "Life is Beautiful" project, the volunteers teamed up to pick up plastic and clear debris from the coastline. This hands-on work helped spread public awareness about keeping our public spaces and oceans clean. After three days of hard work and learning, the camp wrapped up with a closing ceremony and a big group photo by the beach, sending everyone home with great memories and a fresh mindset for social service.

microcontroller-physics.title: Hands-on Physics: Bringing Experiments to Life with SEELab

photos.caption: Students wiring resistors and sensors onto the SEELab 3.0 breadboard
Projected software telemetry interface logging physical sensor values
Analyzing operational amplifier gain alongside kinematics equations
Student hardware presentations demonstrating functional circuit builds

microcontroller-physics.excerpt: A recent educational workshop on microcontroller-based physics experiments provided students with a practical way to connect classroom theory with modern electronics. Instructors walked the class...
paragraphs: A recent educational workshop on microcontroller-based physics experiments provided students with a practical way to connect classroom theory with modern electronics. Instructors walked the class through key principles, exploring concepts like operational amplifier gain alongside kinematics equations used to calculate gravity. To bring these ideas to life and bridge the gap between theory and application, digital software interfaces were projected on screen, showing students exactly how to monitor and log data directly from their upcoming physical setups.

The bulk of the session was highly collaborative and hands-on. Students teamed up to build their own circuits using the SEELab 3.0 open-source science kit, carefully wiring components like resistors directly onto the device's integrated breadboard to connect with various sensors. The environment was engaging and supportive, ultimately culminating in students confidently stepping up to present their completed hardware setups and explain their experimental processes to both the instructors and their peers.

optica-students.title: Inspiring Young Minds: Optics and Light Exploration Outreach

photos.caption: School students testing optical dispersion with glass prisms
Demonstrating light wave convergence and divergence using convex lenses
Hands-on diffraction gratings revealing the visible rainbow spectrum

optica-students.excerpt: Recently, the Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College Chapter of OPTICA organized an engaging educational outreach program designed to advance the understanding of optics and photonics am...
paragraphs: Recently, the Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College Chapter of OPTICA organized an engaging educational outreach program designed to advance the understanding of optics and photonics among school students. The initiative brought together a large, enthusiastic audience of young learners for interactive presentations, including a detailed exploration of the properties of white light. Driven by a dedicated organizing committee and student volunteers, the event successfully fostered a collaborative and interactive environment for the students to explore complex scientific concepts.

During the session, attendees were introduced to foundational science gadgets that transform abstract optical theories into observable physical phenomena. The physics of optical dispersion was demonstrated using glass prisms, which slow down and bend passing light rays at varying angles to separate white light into a visible rainbow spectrum. The program also explored the core principles of refraction using convex and concave lenses to show how light waves can be manipulated to converge at a single focal point or diverge. By interacting with these optical tools alongside diffraction gratings, the students gained a practical, hands-on understanding of photonics and the fundamental behavior of light.

optica-session.title: Exploring Photonics: A Hands-on Look at Optical Gadgets

optica-session.excerpt: The OPTICA Student Chapter at Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College recently hosted an interactive session focused on the mechanics and real-world applications of optical gadgets. Cente...
paragraphs: The OPTICA Student Chapter at Muhammed Abdurahiman Memorial Orphanage College recently hosted an interactive session focused on the mechanics and real-world applications of optical gadgets. Centered around practical demonstrations using "The Optics Suitcase," the program was designed to bring complex concepts in optics and photonics out of theoretical textbooks and into an accessible classroom environment. The workshop provided a collaborative space for students to explore the fundamental principles governing light and vision.

Throughout the event, attendees gained firsthand experience by wearing specialized optical viewing glasses to observe light behavior and spectral patterns. This practical setup allowed the group to test different optical tools simultaneously and actively discuss the visual phenomena unfolding right before their eyes. By bridging the gap between theoretical physics and tangible applications, the chapter successfully fostered a deeper, more engaging understanding of photonics among the participants.
